content: Melvin-Koushki says the lettrist theory of the Mafāḥiṣ deliberately breaks with earlier treatments: Ibn Turka calls the existing literature 'stale and timeworn' and compares it to 'toughened, jerked meat', a reason for not citing earlier authorities, and asserts that lettrism had long been in decline before Akhlāṭī revived it. He tells readers to rid themselves first of standard preconceptions absorbed through imitation of predecessors.
